text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Statoil paid vice president Roger O'Neil 23 million crowns in salary last year to compensate for fringe benefits he had in his previous job with Mobil. Statoil President Harald Norvik earned 1.6 million crowns.
- Vietnamese immigrant children cannot read or write Norwegian after 10 years in a Norwegian school in Lillehammer.
- So far 44 victims of the Russian plane crash on Spitzbergen last month have been identified using DNA technology. The TU-154 slammed into a mountain killing all 141 people on board.
- The Russian ambassador thanks Norway for the salvage operation following last month's crash of a Russian plane on Spitzbergen.
- The Conservative Party and the ruling Labour Party lost ground in the September opinion poll, one year before the next election. But the agrarian-based Centre Party gained support.
- The old 10-crown coin will be invalid from Monday.
- Another Statoil employee is remanded in custody in the Idavoll corruption case.
- Offshore and construction group Aker and investment company RGI may be closer to a merger than what is generally believed.
